cpanel.ag-ri.in (buyer) · quotes.ag-ri.in (vendor portal) · PROCOL DEMO · backend sec-api.ag-ri.in · 29 Oct 2026

Vendor Onboarding E2E Run

Seven onboarding templates built with the Template Studio's own save format, each sent to a fresh QA prospect from cpanel. The prospect filled the form on the vendor portal, and the buyer reviewed it and sent it for approval. Field types, validations, conditional rules, prefill, data sources and multi-section forms were each checked live.

47Pass
13Fail
3Not run
6Bugs

The flow each template went through

Template saved (Studio payload)→Prospect invited + signed up→cpanel: Prospects → Start Onboarding→Vendor: Events → Submission Sheet→Fill, check, Submit→cpanel: Review Pending→Buyer form → Send For Approval
T1All field types — 2 sections: text (required, helper), long text, number, date, dropdown, multi-select, radio, PDF attachment, email, read-only, hiddenT2Validations — PAN (format + PAN check), GSTIN must contain PAN, account number + re-enter (must match, no paste), IFSC format, mobile formatT3Conditional logic — Foreign hides GSTIN; MSME shows + requires Udyam; not Indian requires turnover; company name contains 'Pvt' requires CIN; ISO 9001 requires certificate; Country empty hides StateT4Prefill and data sources — legal name / email / address from the vendor's Procol profile; currency, country, region lists; Country resets Region; supplier code written back to the vendor recordT5Three sections, every field required — text, number, dropdown, date, long text, attachmentT6Empty, number and AND rules (limits saved as text) — Foreign AND turnover > 10 lakh shows SWIFT; employees > 100 requires HR policy; GSTIN not empty requires certificateT7Same as T6 with the limits saved as numbers

Bugs

VOB-01An 'is empty' / 'is not empty' rule crashes the vendor's onboarding formHighVOE-T3-V02, VOE-T3-V06, VOE-T6-V04, VOE-T7-V04
Steps
1. Template with a rule 'Country IS EMPTY → hide State' (or 'GSTIN IS NOT EMPTY → require certificate').
2. Start onboarding for a prospect with it.
3. Vendor opens the form and types anything into Country (or GSTIN).
Expected
State appears (or the certificate becomes required); the form keeps working. On load, State is hidden while Country is empty.
Actual
The whole page is replaced by 'Oops! Something Broke Down…' with 'TypeError: e is not a function' in the console. The vendor cannot fill that field at all. On load the rule also never applies: State is shown while Country is empty. The Studio offers and saves both comparisons, and the backend evaluates them; the form's comparison list has no entry for them.
VOB-02Rules never undo when the vendor changes the answer backHighVOE-T3-V04, VOE-T3-V07, VOE-T7-V03, VOE-T6-V02, VOE-T7-V02
Steps
1. Template T3: Foreign hides GSTIN; MSME shows and requires Udyam; not Indian requires turnover.
2. Vendor picks Foreign, then MSME, then Indian.
Expected
Indian: GSTIN visible again, Udyam hidden, turnover optional (the form returns to the template's default).
Actual
GSTIN stays hidden, so an Indian vendor can never enter the GSTIN the template requires, and Submit goes through without it. Udyam stays visible and required, turnover stays required. Same for numbers: employees 150 → 20 keeps HR policy required; turnover 25 lakh → 9 lakh keeps SWIFT shown. Only a draft Reset restores the form.
VOB-03An AND rule fires when only one of its conditions is trueHighVOE-T6-V02, VOE-T7-V02, VOE-T6-V05, VOE-T7-V05
Steps
1. Template rule: Vendor type IS Foreign AND Annual turnover > 10,00,000 → show and require SWIFT code.
2. Fresh form: choose Foreign with turnover empty. Separately: choose Indian and type 25,00,000.
Expected
SWIFT stays hidden in both cases; it appears only for Foreign with turnover above 10 lakh.
Actual
SWIFT code appears with * in both cases. The form checks only the answer just changed, so an AND rule behaves like OR. Vendors are asked for fields that do not apply to them.
VOB-04'Contains' on a text answer works as 'is exactly' on the vendor formMediumVOE-T3-V05
Steps
1. Template rule: Company name CONTAINS 'Pvt' → require CIN.
2. Vendor types 'QA Steel Pvt Ltd'. Then types exactly 'Pvt'.
Expected
'QA Steel Pvt Ltd' makes CIN required (the Studio preview does this).
Actual
'QA Steel Pvt Ltd' leaves CIN optional. Only the exact text 'Pvt' makes CIN required. The Studio preview and the live form disagree.
VOB-05A number rule compares as text when its limit is saved as textMediumVOE-T6-V03, VOE-T6-V05
Steps
1. Template rule: Number of employees IS GREATER THAN '100' (limit saved as text).
2. Fresh form: type 50, then 99.
Expected
50 and 99 are not more than 100, so HR policy stays optional (the backend compares these as numbers).
Actual
HR policy becomes required for 50 and 99 (text order: '5' > '1'). With the limit saved as the number 100 the same rule works. Which form the Studio saves was not confirmed here, so this matters if any template carries text limits.
VOB-06Attachment limited to PDF accepts a Word fileMediumVOE-T1-V07
Steps
1. Template T1: Company brochure, attachment, allowed type PDF.
2. Vendor uploads brochure.docx and submits.
Expected
The .docx is refused with a message that only PDF is allowed.
Actual
The upload dialog accepts brochure.docx, the field shows it, and the response is submitted with it. The buyer sees 'brochure.d…' in the vendor's answers.

Left on PROCOL DEMO for follow-up

  • The T2D QA vendor was sent for approval to Shivdesh Singh during a dry run of the approval drawer: its last button, Continue, sends the request. The request expires on its own in two days. Requests cannot be withdrawn from the approvals panel.
  • The QA buyer form (B1) was the company's active buyer form from 29 Oct 09:54 until it was removed on 30 Oct; the M3M Gurugram Buyer Form is active again. Vendors sent for approval in that window (T1, T2D, T3 test vendors only) keep B1's copy.
  • Approve and Reject could not be finished. Both go through PROCOL DEMO's approval workflow, and only three named users can approve.

Notes

  • Rule behaviour on the vendor form was checked twice: by the runner, and by probes that reset the draft and reload before every step, so stickiness could not mask a comparison.
  • The saved draft is restored about 7 seconds after the form appears. Anything typed before that is overwritten. Earlier validation runs (T2, T2B, T2C) were affected and are left out; T2D is the clean run.
  • The format mask on PAN does not force capitals; lower-case 'abcde1234f' is kept as typed (and then refused by the format check).
  • The buyer form is copied for each vendor the first time Send For Approval is opened; later changes to the buyer-form template do not reach that vendor.
  • A date set with the calendar's Today button showed on screen but was not saved once (T5); picking a day saved it. Today worked in T1, so this is noted, not filed.
  • Mapped answers (entity mappings, e.g. supplier code) are written to the vendor record only when the onboarding is accepted, not on submit.
  • A required buyer-form dropdown with no options blocks Send For Approval with only 'Please fill …'. This happened with the QA buyer form's payment-terms source, which has no data on PROCOL DEMO; it was switched to the currency list.
  • Creating a buyer-form template makes it the company's active buyer form: the backend picks the newest one. Creating one in the Studio silently replaces the existing form for every new approval.
